name: Can Your Lot Support a Detached ADU?

mainEntity.name: How do I know if my lot can support a detached ADU before paying for full plans?
mainEntity.text: How do I know if my lot can support a detached ADU before paying for full plans?

acceptedAnswer.text: Before investing in full ADU plans, homeowners should request a feasibility review that focuses on the site itself. The most important questions are how much usable yard area exists, where setbacks fall, whether the lot has slope or drainage problems, and how utilities can reach the new unit. Access for construction equipment also matters because it affects both cost and buildability. A contractor familiar with Los Angeles County conditions can flag red flags early, such as easements, retaining wall needs, fire access concerns, or utility relocation. This step can prevent paying for a design that cannot be built as drawn. A strong early review should produce a practical yes, no, or redesign answer before the project moves into expensive engineering and permitting.
acceptedAnswer.description: A lot can usually be screened with a preliminary feasibility review that checks setbacks, access, utility locations, grading, easements, fire clearance, and available buildable area. This early review can show whether a detached ADU is realistic before spending heavily on architectural plans. If the site has tight access or unusual slopes, the design may need to be adjusted.
